topic: The Day London Disappeared into Smog

claims.text: The Great Smog blanketed London from December 5 to December 9, 1952 (5 days).
claims.source_note: UK Met Office Great Smog 1952 archive

claims.text: Residential coal fireplaces and coal power plants released dense soot and sulfur dioxide into humid winter air.
A winter temperature inversion placed warmer air above cooler ground air, trapping emissions near the street.
claims.source_note: UK Met Office temperature inversion explanation

claims.text: Dense smog cut street visibility so buses crawled behind conductors walking ahead with lanterns.
Acidic sulfur and soot droplets irritated airways across densely populated districts.
claims.source_note: UK Met Office health impact note

claims.text: The December 1952 fog caused an estimated 4,000 excess deaths that month.
claims.source_note: London City Hall Great Smog 1952 archive

claims.text: Four years later, the Clean Air Act of 1956 initiated a gradual transition toward smokeless heating.
